d:
Filter chip with an optional count badge. State × Badge.

Used for the expense category filter. Only categories that have data that month are rendered, so the strip length varies. State=Selected is the active filter; Badge=True shows how many entries match.

Selected has its own three tokens (action-chip/selected/*). The other three states still borrow badge/neutral/* and badge/accent/*, which is a loan, not a decision — a filter chip is not a badge. Authorised to finish on 2026-08-19, still open.

Primary action control. Variant × Severity × Size, with State plus orthogonal Disabled and Loading.

Filled = the single main action on a screen. Outline = secondary. Ghost = tertiary and inline actions.

Severity=Danger is only for destructive actions, which must follow the two-tap confirm pattern: first tap shows “¿Eliminar?”, second deletes. Never delete on one tap.

Disabled and Loading are independent axes because they co-occur: a submitting button is both, and an aria-disabled control still takes keyboard focus.

Labels use Control/SM–XL, whose line height is 100% so the text centres in the frame.

Mobile-only entry point for creating records. State = Closed | Open.

Open reveals three FABAction items and dims the page behind with bg/scrim. The plus rotates 45° into a close icon rather than swapping glyphs, so the button never changes shape.

Sits above the bottom nav, not inside it. Only visible on the Mes, Dashboard and Cuentas views — elsewhere there is nothing to create. On desktop the same actions live in MonthNav’s “Agregar” popover.

One item of the FAB speed-dial. Card surface with a border so it separates from the dimmed page behind it.

The icon takes bg/brand — the only colour in the row, which is what makes the three items scannable at a glance.

The three are always Ingreso · Gasto · Movimiento, in that order, staggered 40ms apart from the FAB outward.

Icon-only action. Same four axes as Button.

Row actions are ALWAYS visible — never hidden behind hover (opacity-0 group-hover is an anti-pattern here). Use SM in filter bars and list rows, MD as the default.

Every instance needs an accessible label in code; the icon alone is not a name.

Chip that identifies WHICH account a row belongs to. What KIND of account it is, is AccountTypeBadge’s job; the two answer different questions and can appear together.

The dot carries the account’s accent. At runtime that fill comes from the USER’S DATA — each account stores a hue picked from account/{hue}/accent — so account/purple/accent here is a canvas default, not a decision. Do not “fix” it to a static token: an audit that repoints this to a fixed colour breaks user-chosen account colour.

The body stays neutral on purpose (bg/account · border/subtle · fg/account). Only the dot carries hue, so a row with four chips does not become a colour chart.

The dot sits on bg/account, NOT on the avatar tint, and that is a second background nobody checked until 2026-08-22: amber measured 2.91:1 there and green passed by 0.01. Both moved to rung 700 in light. Any new accent has to clear 3:1 against BOTH.

NOT a component set, deliberately. It used to be one, with Color=Cyan|Purple|Green|Neutral standing in for account slots 1-4; those were renamed to slots, and then the slot model died when the hue became a user choice. What was left were two variant axes with exactly one option each — which is not variance, and would have extracted into code as Color=”Account 4”, a name meaning nothing. Dissolved 2026-08-17; 27 instances verified intact across four pages.

Shipped in code 2026-08-22. The earlier note here said extraction was blocked until the exporter landed — it landed, and this is one of the components it unblocked.

Says what KIND of account this is — Cash, Bank Account, Credit Card, Savings — not which account it is. Which account is AccountBadge’s job; the two chips answer different questions and can appear together.

The four variants map 1:1 to the account types the product supports, so this set gains a variant only when the product gains a type.

Corrected 2026-08-17: this component was carrying AccountBadge’s description verbatim, which claimed its variants were the account/1..4 slots. They never were. (Second instance of a pasted-over description in this file — color/account/border (the pre-1.2 name; today border/subtle) had Input’s.) The rationale line above is reconstructed from the variants themselves; whoever specified the chip should confirm the intent.

2026-09-01 · SIN CONSUMIDORES. AccountCard was its only user and now prints the type as plain text: with its leading icon removed the pill was a border around a single word. Kept, not deleted — absence of use is not absence of purpose, and a labelled type chip is the right shape the day a denser surface needs one. If nothing claims it by the next inventory, retire it.

Generic label chip. Variant × Tone × Icon.

Variant=Filled paints badge/{tone}/background; Variant=Outline paints badge/{tone}/border with no fill. Same geometry, same six token families — this used to be two component sets (Badge filled, Status outline), and the filled one had zero instances in the whole file. Filled and outline are a treatment, not two components.

Outline is the entry-state treatment: scheduled, unconfirmed, overdue. Filled is a plain label.

Colour here is decorative. The moment a badge carries meaning — an account, a category, a currency — use the specific component instead, so the semantic token layer stays the source of that meaning. AccountBadge is the worked example: it exists precisely because a generic Badge was carrying an account name.

One variant per expense category — 15, mapped 1:1 to EGRESO_CATEGORIAS in code.

Colour comes from category/{id}/accent and /surface. In dark mode the surface is -950 and the text -300, uniformly; connectivity and other are the documented exception because their neutral -950 disappears against the page background.
USD or COP marker. Used wherever an amount could be misread as the wrong currency — this product lives in two.

Star toggle on an account. Favourites pin as compact cards on Resumen and sort first in every account picker.

Selected is amber-700, not amber-500. Filling the glyph is what puts it inside WCAG 1.4.11 as a graphic object, not outside it — 500 measured 2.15:1 against white and failed all three backgrounds it can land on.
A 6px dot. Presence marker: unconfirmed entry, unread notification. Carries no colour meaning of its own.
Counter on the header bell. Primary counts overdue and due-today only. Secondary is upcoming (next 7 days) and is deliberately not counted in the badge number.
Live TRM chip in the header. Informative only — every calculation uses the month’s stored TRM, never this one.

Country flag, used to recognise a currency at a glance. Its colours belong to a state, not to us: they stay raw on purpose and must never be tokenised, exactly like the Google mark. The brand-mark/ prefix is what makes C1 skip them by configuration rather than by anyone remembering (design-system/docs/16-marks.md).

Google mark, used on the sign-in button. Its four colours are Google’s, not ours: they are raw hexes ON PURPOSE and must never be bound to a token, because a token implies we are allowed to change them and we are not. They have no dark mode either — the mark is the same in both, which is also why it sits on Brand and not in the Icon Library. Exempt from C1 by CONFIG.foreignBrand; see design-system/docs/16-marks.md. The GitHub mark is the opposite case and is a normal glyph: monochrome, inherits currentColor.

The Neto mark. Style=Primary is the mark on its brand ground; Style=Secondary is the reversed treatment for dark or photographic backgrounds.

Bound to logo/mark and logo/bg, which hold the SAME value in light and dark on purpose: a logo that changes colour with the theme is a different logo. This is identity, not a semantic colour, and it is the one place in the system where mode-invariance is the point.

Account card. Type × State.

Each type shows different data, which is why this is one set and not four components: Bank Account adds the estimated monthly yield, Credit Card shows limit, debt, % used and the cut/payment dates, Savings shows the CDT maturity countdown, Cash has neither number nor rate.

The account type is locked after creation — to reclassify, the account must be recreated. The card never needs to handle a type change.

THE ACCOUNT COLOUR IS THE AVATAR, AND NOTHING ELSE. 2026-09-01: the full-width AccountBanner was removed. It was the card’s only colour and it sat directly above the amount, which is what docs/25-account-color.md §2 forbids in as many words — “cards, rows and amounts stay neutral… an identity colour that only ever appears inside a small circle never shares a surface with a number, so it cannot be mistaken for one.” That boundary is the whole reason twelve hues are safe in an app where cyan already means net, red means expense and amber means tax. The banner also contradicted the code, which has never drawn one.

So the header now opens with an AccountAvatar (size=SM), which is the sanctioned carrier, followed by the account NAME and the favourite star. The account type is PLAIN TEXT in fg/account — a neutral slate, not the account’s hue — and it sits on the META line, between the currency badge and the number.

CORRECTED 2026-09-02. Until today this description, docs/10-account-page.md §10 and the handoff all said the type sat “junto al avatar” in the header, with the name on a line of its own below. Dev built it on the meta line instead and asked. Dev is right, for a reason neither of us wrote down: the name is the account’s identity and the type is a classifier, so a header that leads with the classifier and demotes the identity to the second line has the hierarchy backwards. On the meta line the type also joins the other two classifiers it belongs with — currency and number — and the header stops competing for width.

The name is Body/Small-Emphasis, one line, ellipsis. It truncates: “Bancolombia Ahorros” does not fit beside a 24px avatar and a star inside a 220px card. That is the shipped behaviour, not an oversight, and the sample content is long on purpose so the card is authored against the case that actually happens.

That pairing arrived in two steps. Design first dropped the AccountTypeBadge’s leading icon, because the avatar already draws the type glyph and two identical icons side by side stated the same fact twice. Alfredo then removed the badge altogether on 2026-09-01: once the icon was gone, the outlined pill was a container around a word, and a chip that contains only its own label is a border pretending to be information. AccountTypeBadge now has NO consumer anywhere in the file.

The type still reads as TEXT, which is the form that survives colour blindness and a screen reader — the glyph in the avatar is decorative and announced by nothing. Measured at 11px Medium: 6.92:1 on the default surface, 6.30:1 on selected, 10.99:1 Dark. Small text needs 4.5:1.

BEFORE 2026-09-01 this description said the banner must not be “fixed”. It was written on 08-17, four days before the colour system, and the two decisions had been contradicting each other since. Alfredo settled it on 08-24: the doc wins.

account/purple/accent is the canvas default on the master, not a decision — each account stores its own hue. The palette is twelve account/{hue}/accent + /surface pairs and the picker is AccountColorPicker. Colour lives on the account record; the design system never names an account.

DEPRECATED — superseded by the AccountCard set above. 180×102, no variants, and it duplicated the name of the set, which made both unusable from the asset panel.

Remap any remaining instances to the set, then delete.

Balance over time for one account. Device is the only axis.

A credit card's balance is already ≤ 0, so plotting it as-is draws what is owed growing downward, and the series takes the debt hue. That is the whole of it — there is no second series.

2026-09-02 · Series=Single|Dual was DELETED. Dual's legend read "Cupo · Deuda", and cupo is limit − debt against a limit that does not move, so the second area was the first one mirrored: two shapes, one number. Measured before removing it: four instances in the file, all four inside this component's own documentation, none on a screen. Dev asked what number Dual plotted, which was the right question — the description named the picture and never the quantity. If a real second quantity ever exists, the axis comes back with a reason attached.

Both series carry a gradient that fades to fully transparent — account-chart/series/*/fill-to is the same hue at 0 alpha, not white — so the fill never turns milky over a dark canvas.

The marker line is account-chart/marker/line: slate on light, white at 70% on dark, because one fixed grey disappears against one of the two.

2026-09-01 · the static "Últimos 30 días" label was removed from the header. The range is now stated by chart-range, the strip of pills under the chart, and the axis already prints the dates. A fixed label would have contradicted both the moment anyone picked a different range — and a label that can contradict the control next to it is worse than no label.

The header card of an account page: name, type and the headline balance. Type follows the account kinds (Bank Account · Cash · Credit Card · Savings) and Device switches the desktop and mobile layouts.

2026-09-01: the OPEN item is closed. The icon was a bare Icon Account painted with account-summary-card/icon/foreground — a fixed purple that could not follow the account. It is now an AccountAvatar (size=SM), the same carrier the account card and the colour picker use, so the account page shows the colour its owner chose. account-summary-card/icon/foreground has no consumer left.

The generic surface everything else sits on. Footer = True/False.

Slots: header (title + description), content, footer. The footer carries a top border and is the only part that is optional.

This is the base of AccountCard, SavingsCard and SectionCard — if the card chrome changes, it changes here.

Where the gross income of the month went, as one bar. Not a chart component — it always shows the same four segments in the same order: Obligaciones · Provisiones · Gastos · Neto libre.

Segments come from chart/categorical/*, so a segment can never drift from the KPI card it corresponds to. Hovering one dims the rest to 40% and reveals its amount on the right.

Segments with a zero amount are not rendered, so the bar can have between one and four.

Dashboard KPI tile: label, figure, secondary line. The figure is Amount/Hero — it was bound to Heading/Section, a heading style on money, which the typography spec forbids (§3: money always takes an Amount/* style). The strip’s five figures are the ones a user opens the app to read.

A single figure with its label. Sub = True/False.

Sits on bg/subtle, not on a card — it is meant to be embedded inside another card, not to stand alone. That is what separates it from KPI-Card, which is a control you can click.

The figure uses Amount/Large; the label Detail/Large.

Savings account card. Type × State × Size.

Only savings-type accounts appear in the Ahorros view. CDT variants show a maturity countdown — Show Maturity is live on Type=CDT and controls three nodes; it was nearly deleted on 2026-08-20 by a scan that sampled only the first variant of the set.

Known inconsistency: the variant values are still Spanish (Cuenta | CDT | Inversión) while every other set in the file is English. Worth normalising when this set is next touched.

RETIRED 2026-09-02 — LEGACY. Do not build with it and do not extend it.

Alfredo: the Savings page no longer exists. Every account lives on the accounts page now, whatever its type, and the card that represents one is AccountCard — including CDTs and savings accounts, which is what this component was for.

It stays in the file for the same reason AccountCard (legacy) does: something on a screen may still point at it, and deleting a component that a frame still instantiates replaces the frame's content with nothing and says why nowhere. It is renamed rather than removed so that anyone who lands on it knows before they copy it.

What replaces what: SavingsCard → AccountCard with Type=Savings. The CDT-specific figures it carried — maturity, rate — are metrics on AccountSummaryCard on the account's own page, not on the tile.

THE most used container in the product — 10 files import it. Action = True/False.

A Card with an icon + title header and an optional action on the right. The title uses Heading/Group, which is the most common header in the app precisely because of this component.

Every list section in the Mes view is one of these: Ingresos, Gastos, Movimientos, Tributarias, Provisiones.

The Gastos tab — the largest container in the system: category chips with counts, sort and filters, and a distribution bar.

The strip of category chips only renders categories that have data that month, so its length changes month to month and the layout has to survive one chip or fifteen.

The Ingresos tab of the Mes view.

Lists the month’s incomes with account badges and a gross total converted with that month’s TRM.

The ledger card of an account page: every movement, in date order, and nothing else.

IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE PAGE WAS BORROWING IncomeContainer, which is the Ingresos tab of the Mes view. That component opens with an icon and the title “Ingresos del mes” and closes with a converted monthly gross — two things a ledger has neither of. The account IS the title, and the number that matters is the running balance, not a monthly sum.

IT HAS NO HEADER, and losing it is the point. The first build gave it one, and putting it on the real screen showed that four of its six items already sat in the AccountSummaryCard above: the account name, the edit affordance, “16% usado · Corte 4 · Pago 20”, and the current debt. Of the two that did not repeat, Alfredo cut both on 2026-09-01 and was right about each:

· the movement count was noise on a list you can see;
· Entradas and Salidas summed the ENTIRE ledger, every month of it, and sat directly under a chart labelled “Últimos 30 días”. Two different time scales on one screen, neither of them saying so. A figure whose period is invisible is worse than no figure, because it invites a comparison that does not hold.

With the header gone BOTH AXES LOST THEIR REASON. Balance=Deuda|Saldo existed to switch the headline label and its colour; Device existed to hide the Entradas/Salidas pair on a phone. Neither has anything left to switch, so this is one component and not a set of four. A variant that changes nothing is a variant nobody maintains. Device now lives entirely in the rows, where it belongs.

The opening balance is no longer a strip above the list: it is a ledger-itemrow in State=Opening, the LAST row, because the ledger runs newest first. That is what makes the card one table instead of a table with a lid — it takes the same rules, the same left rail and the same right edge as the movements it explains.

Rows arrive through the Rows SLOT, which prefers ledger-itemrow and accepts nothing else. Each row draws its own bottom rule and the last one is switched off by hand: CSS has last:border-0 and Figma has no last-child selector, so that override must be re-applied whenever the number of rows changes.

The sample figures reconcile, on purpose: 1.541.300 opening + 543.200 out − 800.000 in = 1.284.500, and the scheduled entry does not move the balance. Sample content that does not add up cannot be used to review anything.

The Provisiones tab: primas, cesantías, vacaciones, computed on gross income with provisions enabled.

Conditional in the same way as TaxContainer. Users can add their own provisions, so the list length is not fixed.

The Tributarias tab: salud, pensión, ARL and retención, plus the FSS row that appears automatically when IBC ≥ 4 SMMLV.

Conditional — the whole tab is absent for the empleado profile. Also holds the payment calendar keyed to the last digits of the cédula.
The Movimientos tab. Transfers between own accounts, with the effective-TRM calculator.

Empty state for a list that has no entries yet. Media = Icon | None.

The dashed border is deliberate: it says “this container is real but has nothing in it”, which a solid border would not. It is the one place in the system that uses a dash.

Always carries an action. An empty state without a way out is a dead end.

Something failed and has to be retried. Sibling of Empty: same anatomy, different intent.

The border is SOLID on purpose. Empty’s dashed border means “a real container, but empty” and is the only dash in the system; an error is not empty.

The media uses bg/danger-subtle with the icon in fg/danger — the tint, not the emphasis: a failed load is not a catastrophe.

The description reminds the reader that the data is still on the device. The app is local-first and a view failure puts nothing saved at risk.

A bar that says how far along something is. Track in bg/neutral-subtle, fill in the tone, 8 high, both ends fully rounded.

It exists because two unrelated surfaces needed it and neither had it. A credit card’s utilisation is computed in calc.ts and printed as bare text — “16% usado” — with nothing to see; and the retención reserve needs caused-against-reserved with the gap as the headline. Two consumers that share nothing but the shape is the definition of a system piece rather than a one-off (Rule 11).

IT IS NOT DistribucionCard. That is a breakdown — four fixed segments of one whole, always the same four, and its job is composition. This is one quantity against one limit. They look alike and mean different things, which is exactly why they are two components and not a variant axis.

TWO TONES, AND ONLY TWO, because there are two consumers:
· Provision — progress toward something you are building up. The reserve.
· Expense — a limit being consumed. Credit utilisation.

Neutral, Warning and Danger are deliberately NOT minted. Nothing asks for them yet, and a threshold (“turn red past 80%”) is a product rule this component should not own — the consumer picks the tone, the bar draws it.

WARNING WOULD NOT WORK AS DRAWN, and this is worth knowing before anyone adds it. bg/tax is amber/400 and measures 1.52:1 against the track in Light. A bar carries its meaning by its boundary, so 1.4.11 applies and asks for 3:1. That is the third place today amber/400 has come up short — the ss glyph and the account dot were the other two. A warning tone has to come from a darker amber rung, not from bg/tax.

Measured fill-against-track, Light · Dark: Provision 3.44 · 7.61. Expense 3.44 · 5.29. Both clear 3:1 in both modes, and Light is the tight one.

IT NEVER APPEARS WITHOUT ITS NUMBER. Length and colour are the only things the bar carries, so on its own it fails 1.4.1 and is unreadable to anyone who cannot compare two lengths precisely. Both consumers already print the figure — “16% usado”, the gap in pesos — and that is a requirement, not a coincidence.

THE VALUE IS SET WITH layoutGrow, NOT BY RESIZING, and that is forced by Figma rather than chosen. Inside an instance a child’s WIDTH cannot be overridden — `resize` runs, returns no error and changes nothing, the same silent refusal `maxWidth` gives. `layoutGrow` is overridable, so the bar is two children that split the track: `fill` at the percentage and `remainder` at what is left. Set both — 16 and 84 — and the bar reads 16%.

AT 100% THE REMAINDER IS HIDDEN, not set to zero. A layoutGrow of 0 does not collapse a child — Figma falls back to its last width, so a “full” bar drew at 63%. Hiding it is the only thing that empties it. Same for 0%: hide `fill`.

It is not a variant axis because a percentage is continuous; 101 variants is not a component. And the track clips, so anything past 100% draws as full: if a reserve can exceed what it covers, the bar cannot say so and the number has to.

A 1px rule on border/default.

Only for separating peers inside one container. Between containers the gap does the work — a rule there reads as a border that failed.

Loading placeholder. Uses bg/disabled — the same token as a disabled control, because both mean “here but not usable yet”.

Matches the shape of what is coming, never a spinner. A spinner tells you to wait; a skeleton tells you what you are waiting for.

Work in progress after a user action. Does NOT replace Skeleton: a skeleton says what content is coming, and can only do so when there is a shape to anticipate. When someone presses a button there is nothing to anticipate — the only thing to confirm is that the click was handled.

Colour: prefer INHERITING. A spinner inside a control should take currentColor for the head and currentColor at 20% for the track, so it can never disagree with the label beside it — a danger outline button has a red label and neither fixed tone is red. spinner/head/on-solid and /default exist for a spinner standing alone with no label to inherit from.

Renamed 2026-08-22: the tokens were on-dark / on-light, which named the BUTTON and not the surface — their values invert between modes, so on-dark was light in light mode. Dev found it.

Rotation: motion/duration/spin on motion/easing/spin.

Transient confirmation. Inverts against the page via bg/inverse + fg/on-inverse.

Centred at the bottom, above the mobile nav and above any open sheet — it has to stay visible over a drawer.

No action, no dismiss button. If the user needs to do something about it, it is not a toast.

The twelve account colours, two rows of six, spread across the full width of whatever holds them.

No caption and no colour name on screen. Choosing an account colour is a preference, not a task with a right answer, so nothing is lost when two hues are hard to tell apart — and the selection is carried by a check mark, not by colour, so 1.4.1 is satisfied without words. The names survive as each swatch’s accessible name.

No “in use” marker. Colours repeat across accounts by design; an unexplained dot on a choice with no wrong answer reads as a restriction.

Ordered by hue — warm, green, cyan, blue, violet, pink — so the two closest pairs sit adjacent and read as two colours rather than as one met twice.

Two explicit rows, not a wrapping grid: wrap packs as many as fit and becomes eight per row at this width. Six per row is a decision.

Carries no label of its own. Wrap it in Field.

One colour a user can pick for an account. The chip is the accent at full strength; the tint the avatar uses is a separate token and is not shown here, because it is invisible against a light canvas.

Geometry: 44px hit target, 36px disc, radius/full. 44 rather than the 40 it started at — these sit close together and the minimum is a floor, not a target. The 4px inset is the gap the selection ring needs so a ring in the same accent still reads as a ring.

Selected draws a 2px ring in the account’s own accent. Not the brand colour: the ring has to survive eleven other hues beside it. Hover is a neutral 1px border/strong ring — a hover ring in the accent is one step from reading as selected.

Every swatch needs an accessible name (Morado · Celeste · Esmeralda · Lima · Ámbar · Fucsia · Azul · Verde · Índigo · Naranja · Rosa · Turquesa). The name is not shown; a screen-reader user still has to hear one.

Ordered by HUE ANGLE, measured from each accent’s Light value: orange 21° · amber 32 · lime 86 · green 142 · emerald 161 · teal 175 · sky 200 · blue 221 · indigo 243 · purple 271 · pink 333 · rose 347.

The order is not decoration. The neighbours are the pairs that measure closest — orange/amber at 11°, emerald/teal at 14 — and sitting them side by side is what lets someone SEE they are two colours, instead of meeting the second one six positions later and reading it as the first again.

One account in the onboarding list. The leading check is not a choice: it says the account is included, and it is always on — what varies is whether the user can take it out.

Type=Fixed is an account the product includes and nobody can remove (Efectivo). Type=User is one the person added: it carries the brand wash, the primary border and the remove button. The difference in weight is deliberate — it marks what is theirs.

Show badge turns on the currency chip; Show description the second line. Focused is the two-ring shadow, clipped behind the node so it does not tint the translucent fill (see 19-choice-rows.md).

Month grid inside the date popover. DatePicker was retired into Field + Input on 2026-08-20, so the popover now belongs to a date-configured Input, not to a component of its own. Spanish weekday initials, Monday first — es-CO, not the Sunday-first US default.

One selected day, today outlined. Days outside the month are dimmed but still pickable.

Single day cell in the Calendar month grid.

State is a property, not a baked layer — hover, focus-visible and disabled exist here and nowhere else. “outside” days belong to the adjacent month and remain pickable, so they are active text and meet 4.5:1.

The date range of an account chart — the strip of pills under it, the pattern every stocks app uses.

It composes Segment instances rather than minting a pill of its own. Segment’s own description says a segment on its own is not a control; this is one of the controls that composes them, the same relationship tab-navigation has with Tab. Selected therefore reuses Segment’s Selected — bg/brand-alpha-20 with border/brand-alpha-50 — so “selected” means the same thing here as in every other control in the file.

THE STRIP IS VARIABLE LENGTH, AND THAT IS THE RULE, NOT A CONVENIENCE. A range is rendered only when the account has at least one movement OLDER than that range’s start. Otherwise it draws exactly the same line as the shorter range beside it, and a control that cannot change what you see is not a choice — it is a promise the data does not keep. Alfredo’s call, 2026-09-01, and it is the reason the full seven can be offered at all.

Two of the seven need something the data model does not guarantee. `date` is OPTIONAL on an income (src/types), so an account whose movements only carry a month has no day-level series at all: 1D and 1S cannot be drawn for it and must not be offered. 5A waits the same way — the app is younger than five years, so the pill appears the first time an account is.

That is why this is a strip of instances and not a variant axis. Its length is data, not design, exactly as tab-navigation’s is (Tributarias and Provisiones only exist when the user enabled those groups) and action-chip’s is (only categories with data that month).

AccountChart lost its static “Últimos 30 días” label the day this arrived. The strip now states the range, the axis already prints the dates, and a fixed label would have contradicted both the moment anyone picked 1A.

OPEN — two copy choices Alfredo should settle: “1S” for the week (mirrors the reference’s 1W; “7D” is less ambiguous in Spanish) and “YTD”, kept as the acronym Colombian finance uses, where “Año” would be plainer.

The pills are 32 high, like every Segment. That clears 2.5.8 (24) and not 2.5.5 (44); it is the height the rest of the system already uses for this control, so changing it is a decision about Segment, not about this strip.

A single choice among options, drawn as a row. It is a radio in row form: the choice is exclusive and the state lives in the group, so it carries the system Radio instead of drawing its own mark.

Show media turns on the leading tile — use it when the options are kinds of thing rather than values, because an icon is what gets scanned before the words. Show description turns on the second line; a row with no description is a value, a row with one is a decision.

State and Selected are separate axes and are visible at the same time. Focused is the two-ring shadow, the same one CurrencyRadio uses; it never replaces the selection.

Choosing one currency among several, in card form. It is a radio, not a button: the choice is exclusive and the state lives in the group, not in the card. That is why it carries the system Radio inside instead of drawing its own mark.

The flag is not decoration: in an app that shows two currencies at once, it is what gets recognised before anything is read. Its colours stay raw on purpose — they belong to a country, not to us — so it lives in brand-mark/flag, exempt from C1 (see design-system/docs/16-marks.md).

Selected=True paints bg/brand-alpha-10 with a bg/brand border; State=Focused is the ring and never replaces the selection: you can be focused without having chosen, and both have to be visible at once.

A form field: the label, the control, and the message. Built 2026-08-20 because the system had four form components and four different answers about labels — Input, Select and DatePicker had none at all and were letting the placeholder do the job, at 2.56:1 contrast and gone as soon as the user types.

The control is an INSTANCE SWAP: swap in Input, Select or anything else — including an Input configured as a date or money field, which is what replaced DatePicker and MoneyInput. The field’s own visual state (focus, disabled) belongs to the control; this wrapper only knows whether the message is a hint or an error.

The control slot HUGS. It was FIXED at 40px — the height of an Input — which silently clipped anything taller the moment one was swapped in: AccountColorPicker lost its second row and the drawer looked like it had six colours. An instance-swap slot cannot carry the height of its default occupant.

Text field. HasValue × State × Size.

MD (36px) is the standard for every form. SM (28px) belongs to filter bars only. All controls in the same row must share a size — an input, a select and a date picker side by side at different heights is the most common visual bug in this product.

Overflow: the value fills the remaining width and truncates with an ellipsis; the icons hug and never shrink. A value longer than the field must not widen it.

Single choice within a group. 20px, 2px ring, filled with bg/brand and a check when selected.

Selected is also what a locked, always-on row looks like — the “Efectivo” account in onboarding is drawn with this, not with a separate indicator, because it means the same thing to the reader: this one is in.

No Disabled and no Hover: nothing in Neto disables one option of a group, and the whole row is the hit target, so the ring itself never carries a hover. Both come back as decisions if a screen needs them.

Created 2026-08-17 while mapping the onboarding flow, where this was hand-rolled five times.

One segment of a segmented control. Compose them inside SegmentedControl — a segment on its own is not a control.

Selected paints bg/brand with primary-foreground text; Default and Hover have no fill and differ only in text colour. There is deliberately NO Disabled state: the two segmented controls in the product (account type, currency) never disable a segment, and designing one would be inventing a state nobody asked for.

Built 2026-08-17 from OnboardingView.tsx, where this control was hand-rolled twice out of raw button elements with two different paddings. This unifies them at 10/6; if a tighter one is genuinely needed it comes back as a Size property, not as a second drawing.

Segmented control: a small, flat set of mutually exclusive choices, all visible at once. Use it when the options are few and comparable; use Select when they are many or long.

Items=3 is the account-type picker (Cuenta · Efectivo · Crédito), Items=2 is the currency picker (COP · USD). Segments FILL the track, so every option is the same width and the control reads as one object rather than as buttons in a row — resize the instance, do not resize the segments.

Geometry: container radius/full, bg/chrome with a border/subtle hairline, padding spacing/4, gap spacing/2. The selected segment is bg/brand-alpha-20 with a border/brand-alpha-50 border and fg/on-subtle text — a wash, not a solid fill. A solid brand fill forces white text and makes the control the loudest thing on screen, which is wrong for a picker inside a form. Both states are 34px because the border is always drawn, transparent when inactive; otherwise selecting shifts its neighbours by 1px.

Dropdown trigger. Deliberately shares the axes and heights of Input so the two align in a row.

In code the height comes from the size prop or from data-size=“none” — never from an h-* class, which loses to the data-attribute specificity and silently does nothing.

Overflow: the value fills the remaining width and truncates with an ellipsis; the icons hug and never shrink. A value longer than the field must not widen it.

Toggle for a boolean setting. State × Disabled.

Track 36×20, thumb 16. The off track is an alpha (black 20% light / white 30% dark) so it reads on any surface — a solid grey would disappear on a card and shout on the page background.

Used for “aplicar provisiones”, “gasto recurrente” and the deduction toggles. Never for an action — a switch commits immediately, it has no confirm step.

Tab in the Mes view navigation: Ingresos · Gastos · Movimientos · Tributarias · Provisiones.

The last two only exist when the user has that deduction group enabled, so the strip must read correctly with three tabs or five. Do not design for five and hope.

An account’s identity mark: the tinted circle in account/{hue}/surface with the account-type glyph in account/{hue}/accent. This is the pairing the colour picker is choosing, and the only place the surface token is used.

Two axes. Colour is twelve. size is SM (24) and LG (40) — SM because both consumers needed it, AccountCard’s header and AccountSummaryCard’s. MD (32) exists in the code’s cva and is deliberately NOT minted here: nothing uses it yet, and a variant with no consumer is a variant nobody maintains.

The account TYPE stays a nested swap (Icon Account: Bank Account · Cash · Credit Card · Savings) rather than a variant axis. Twelve colours times four types would be 48 variants for two independent decisions — colour is the user’s, type is the account’s.

THE COST OF THAT NESTING, found 2026-09-01 and worth knowing before you change a type. The accent is bound on the glyph’s VECTOR, three instance levels down, and each account type resolves to a DIFFERENT vector. So switching Account Type on an instance lands on a glyph that still carries the icon library’s own fg/subtle, and the account colour silently disappears. Figma has no inheritance; the code does — it sets --account-accent on the span and the glyph inherits it — which is why this is a Figma-only trap. Whoever switches the type on an instance must re-bind that glyph’s fill to account/{hue}/accent. Every instance in the file is bound correctly today.

Glyph contrast is verified against its own tint in both modes: Light floor 3.07:1, Dark floor 8.02:1. A filled glyph is a graphic object, so 1.4.11 applies — the rule the favourite star was got wrong on.

The twelve are ordered by HUE ANGLE, measured from each accent’s Light value: orange 21° · amber 32 · lime 86 · green 142 · emerald 161 · teal 175 · sky 200 · blue 221 · indigo 243 · purple 271 · pink 333 · rose 347. Read as a ramp it lands almost back where it started, which is what a wheel does.

The order is not decoration. Neighbours are the pairs that measure closest — orange/amber at 11°, emerald/teal at 14 — and putting them side by side is what lets someone SEE they are two, instead of meeting one of them six positions later and reading it as the same colour twice. The CHILD order in the set is that ramp. Figma’s properties panel is not: it keeps its own option order (purple first, today), it has done so since before the size axis was added, and reordering the children does not re-derive it. The description used to claim the panel was sorted too. It never was.
User avatar, SM–XL. Falls back to initials on the avatar/background token when there is no image.

Sized wrapper around a Lucide glyph. size = XS 12 · S 16 · M 20 · L 24, bound to icon-size/*.

The glyph itself is the Glyph property — an instance swap wired to the 76 icons on the Icons page. Change the glyph there, never by detaching.

Every icon in the product goes through this component, which is why size is a variant and not a manual resize: an icon at 17px is a bug, not a choice.

Account-type glyph. One variant per account type — Bank Account, Cash, Credit Card, Savings — so the icon can never disagree with the account type it sits next to.

size is S (16) and XS (12). XS was added 2026-09-01 for AccountAvatar’s SM. It is a real master per type, not a resize: the first attempt set size=XS as an OVERRIDE on the nested Icon inside the avatar, which pinned that Icon’s whole property set, so switching Account Type afterwards fell back to the Glyph property’s default and every non-default type drew a plus sign. A size that changes geometry belongs in a master, never in an override two levels up.

The tinted bubble that opens every ledger row: a 32px circle in a subtle background token with a 16px glyph in the matching foreground token. Seven types, one nested swap — putting them on the row instead would multiply every row state by seven for a decision the entry already carries.

Two glyphs do double duty. income and transfer-in share arrow-down-left; egreso and transfer-out share arrow-up-right. Colour is the only thing separating each pair inside the bubble, so it is never the only carrier in use: the row prints “Desde {cuenta}” or “Hacia {cuenta}” for a transfer and the entry description for the rest (WCAG 1.4.1).

scheduled OVERRIDES the type rather than sitting beside it. A scheduled entry shows the clock on the neutral tint whatever it is underneath, because at that point what matters is that it has not happened yet. The row also drops to 60% and prints the “Programado” badge.

Glyph contrast is measured against its own tint in both modes: Light floor 3.58:1 (income), Dark floor 5.84:1 (egreso). A filled glyph is a graphic object, so 1.4.11 applies.

Type=opening is the seventh, added 2026-09-01, and it is the only one that is not a movement: it marks the account’s STARTING balance at the foot of the ledger. It takes the wallet glyph on the neutral tint — wallet because it is the account itself rather than anything that happened to it, and neutral because the five movement colours all mean a direction and this has none. It deliberately avoids landmark, which Icon Account already uses for a bank account, and the two arrows, the clock and the shield, which are taken.

The glyph is 16 (icon-size/md), not the 14 the code passes. 14 is not a rung on the icon scale — 12 · 16 · 20 · 24 — and a one-off would flatten the scale for one row.

OPEN for Dev: the ss bubble in code paints its glyph with --color-tax, which resolves to bg/tax (amber/400) and measures 1.61:1 on amber/50 in Light. That fails 1.4.11. Figma uses fg/tax (amber/700, 4.84:1); the published name is --color-tax-txt.
Mobile tab bar, 412×58. The FAB with its speed-dial sits above it, not inside it.
A single bottom-nav tab.

Hierarchical navigation between pages. The last crumb is the current page and is not a link.

Levels = how many crumbs are shown. More than 4 is not supported: if the path is deeper, collapse the middle segments before reaching this component — the breadcrumb does not truncate on its own.

The house icon lives in the first crumb and is off by default, because only the root carries it.

Tokens: breadcrumb/* in the Component collection, all aliases, both modes.

One crumb. Type=Link is navigable; Type=Current is the current page, marked with aria-current, and therefore only exists in State=Default — it does not react to the pointer and does not take focus.

State documents the link states: Default, Hover (underline plus a darker foreground), Focus (a 2px ring drawn outside, over the 4px padding that exists precisely to house it).

The 4px padding-x is not decoration: it is the box of the focus ring. Removing it makes the ring cut through the letters.

A sidebar row. State × Expanded.

40px tall, 12px radius, px-3 py-2 expanded and p-3 centred when collapsed.

Selected is cyan. Hover stays neutral on purpose: two cyan states next to each other read as two selections.

Naming nit, still open: the State values mix casing (Selected | default | disabled | hover).

Month stepper at the top of the Mes view.

The arrows are the only way to change month — there is no date picker here, because the app is built around one month at a time and jumping is rare.

Prev is disabled in January and next in December: the store holds one calendar year, so there is nowhere to step to. Touch targets are 44px on mobile and 32px on desktop.

Desktop adds the “Agregar” popover, which carries the same three actions the FAB carries on mobile. Title is Heading/Subsection — the code had 17px bold, snapped to the 18px scale step.

Full-height navigation panel. The panel itself is square (radius/none) — it is flush to the viewport edge, so a corner radius there would read as a floating card, which it is not. The rows are menu-item instances (radius/16 on a 40px row).

One step of the onboarding stepper. Done is interactive — you can go back — which is why it alone has a hover; Current and Pending are not.

Show Connector is false on the last item only. The connector belongs to the item rather than the parent so the stepper can wrap without leaving a line pointing at nothing.

The onboarding wizard rail. It reports progress AND what has been chosen so far, because in a three-step flow where every step is optional and pre-filled, “how far along am I” is a weak question — the answer is always “almost done” — and “what am I actually keeping” is the useful one.

That second line matters in Neto specifically: the flow lets you skip any step. A rail that shows the value makes the consequence visible.

State is carried by silhouette, not only by hue: Done is filled with a check, Current is a ring with a solid dot, Pending is an empty ring. Colour alone would leave Current and Pending indistinguishable to anyone who cannot separate the two tints. The connector line is the redundant encoding of the same progress — not decoration.

Desktop only. On mobile the bar stays: no room for a rail, and none for the value line either.

The Mes view tab strip, composed of Tab instances.

Its length is variable: Tributarias and Provisiones only exist when the user has those deduction groups enabled.

Header bar, 54px.

Holds the live TRM chip, the notification bell, the theme toggle and the account menu. Configuración and Perfil live in that menu, not in the main navigation — which is why the nav shows four destinations for five surfaces.

The colour section of the account edit drawer — the part that feature adds, not the whole form. Name, type, currency, number and balance already exist above it in code and are not redrawn here.

Two things it fixes in place: the live AccountAvatar shows what the choice produces, so the picker chips do not have to preview the tint themselves; and the picker is wrapped in Field, so its label comes from the same place every other label in Neto does.

Floating panel anchored to a trigger. 288px wide.

Desktop only — on mobile the same content opens in a Sheet, because a popover near the bottom of a phone screen ends up under the thumb or off-screen.

Uses bg/anchored, which is a separate elevation rung from the card surface, so a popover over a card still reads as a layer above it.

One line of a data readout: chip, label, figure.

Divider draws the hairline ABOVE the row, so grouping is a property of the row that starts a group rather than a fake blank item between two rows. Dim is the muted state for a line that is present but not in play.

Swatch hides the chip for a line that names no series — a total, a note.

The chip is readout/swatch/*, which is deliberately the same value in Light and Dark: the surface underneath it flips, so a mode-following colour would land on the surface it was not chosen against.

Mobile action menu for a list row. State = Default | Confirming.

Every row is a Button at Size=XL, and the variant carries the consequence: Editar is Outline · Neutral, Eliminar is Outline · Danger, and Cancelar is Ghost · Neutral in its own group under a rule. Deleting escalates in place — Confirming turns Eliminar into Filled · Danger and rewrites it to “Tocar para confirmar eliminación”. Outline → filled is the whole confirmation: same button, same position, more weight.

There is no modal, and the sheet stays open between the two taps, so the user never loses sight of which entry they are deleting.

Prominence tracks consequence here, which is deliberate and has a cost worth knowing: the destructive action is the most visible thing in the sheet in both states and the way out is the quietest. That is the right order for a menu the user opened on purpose. It is the wrong order for one they opened by accident, and this sheet is reachable by a mis-tap on a row — if that turns out to bite, the fix is to give Cancelar an outline, not to quieten Eliminar.

Delete is optional. A row with nothing to delete — an account's opening balance is a field on the account, not an entry — hides the action rather than showing it as a no-op.

Desktop uses inline row actions instead; this component does not appear there.

The panel every form opens in. Device × Footer.

Mobile slides up from the bottom with a drag handle and rounds its top corners. Desktop slides in from the right and rounds only the left side. Different patterns, not a reflow — that is why Device is a variant and not a breakpoint.

The scrim behind it is bg/scrim, not part of this component. On mobile the sheet is clamped to the visual viewport so the keyboard never covers the fields.

The sheet owns the chrome and nothing else: handle, header, close, and the footer's frame. What fills it comes from two openings. Content is an instance-swap — SheetContent is its default and exists only because an instance-swap needs a component as one; AccountEditForm is the first real occupant. Footer content is a slot, added by Alfredo 2026-09-02, so the actions at the bottom stop being drawn into the component.

Footer and Footer content are two questions, not one: the variant says WHETHER there is a footer, the slot says WHAT is in it. The slot was called "footer" for a few hours and renamed on 2026-09-02, because two properties that differ only in case are two properties nobody can tell apart out loud.

Content was added 2026-08-21. Before it, the body held a text node and an instance cannot have children added or removed, so every flow that needed a real form had to detach the sheet.

The default occupant of Sheet’s Content slot. Swap it for the real form. It exists so Sheet has something to swap: an instance-swap property needs a component as its default, and a bare text node cannot be one.

Short explanation on hover or focus. Side = where it sits relative to the trigger, which is also where the arrow points.
Inverts against the page — bg/inverse with fg/on-inverse — so it reads as an overlay and never as part of the content underneath.

Content is an INSTANCE_SWAP, the same shape Sheet uses. The bubble owns the surface, the arrow, the cap at 320 and the inversion; what goes inside it is swappable. TooltipText is the default sentence. TooltipReadout is the data readout a chart needs. Forking the bubble to carry a table would have duplicated the inversion in two places.

Desktop only: there is no hover on touch. Anything a mobile user needs to know must be visible without one — for a chart that means the selected point's figures belong in the card's own metrics, not only in this bubble.

A data readout: a titled list of series, each one a colour chip, a label and a figure. It goes inside Tooltip · Content.

It is a separate component and not a Tooltip variant because only the CONTENT differs — the surface, the arrow, the inversion and the cap are the same object. Splitting it that way keeps the inversion defined once.

Rows is a slot that takes ReadoutRow. Title is the point being read — a date on a chart, the metric's name on a KPI.

The chips do not use the chart's own series colours. Those are chosen against the card; this sits on bg/inverse, which is the opposite surface. See readout/swatch/*.

The default occupant of Tooltip · Content: one short sentence, Body/Small on fg/on-inverse.

It exists because an instance-swap property needs a component as its default and a bare text node cannot be one — the same reason SheetContent exists.

Legend entry for the annual donut and the 8-month trend bars.

Colour comes from chart/categorical/1–5, which alias the KPI tokens — so a legend swatch can never drift from the KPI it labels.

Income row. State=Pressed is the mobile tap feedback (the row is a button on mobile, a static line on desktop); State=Confirming is the desktop inline delete confirmation, where the danger icon button is replaced by a filled danger button reading “¿Eliminar?”.

The account chip is AccountBadge, not a generic Badge: it carries the account’s colour dot.

One entry in an account’s ledger. The five sibling rows each show one KIND of thing in its own view; this one shows whatever the account did, in date order, so a single row has to carry an income, an expense, both legs of a transfer and a social-security payment.

That is why the leading mark is a nested LedgerEntryIcon swap and not an axis. Six entry types times the axes below would be sixty variants for a fact the entry already carries.

Three axes, and the matrix is deliberately sparse:
· Device — Desktop edits and deletes in place; Mobile opens RowActionsSheet behind one button.
· Flow — Credit prints the sign and paints the amount fg/provision; Debit leaves it fg/default. This is the one thing the siblings never needed, because each of them only ever moves money one way.
· State — Default, Scheduled, Confirming, Opening. Confirming is Desktop only: it is the inline delete confirmation, and Mobile confirms inside the sheet. There is no Pressed, which the siblings do have, because this row has no pressed styling in code — the mobile tap opens the sheet and nothing else happens.

Scheduled is a state of the ENTRY, not of the row: the whole row drops to 60%, the mark becomes the clock whatever the type underneath, and the “Programado” badge appears on the metadata line.

THE BADGE SITS ON THE METADATA LINE, not beside the description, and that is the row family’s answer rather than a preference. The first build put it next to the description and capped the description with maxWidth so the badge could never be squeezed. That cap cannot survive: maxWidth is one of the few properties Figma refuses to override per instance, so a cap authored for a 603 row still truncated at 942, where the account page actually uses it. outcome-itemrow had already solved it — description alone on its line, FILL, truncating, no cap; badges and date below as chips that hug. It adapts to any width because nothing is pinned.

State=Opening is the account’s STARTING balance, and it is a row rather than the strip it used to be above the list. That is the whole change: as a strip it had its own background and its own edges and read as a lid on the table; as a row it takes the same rules, the same left rail and the same right edge as the movements it explains, so the card is one table. It sits LAST, because the ledger runs newest first.

It carries the same mark and the same trailing actions as every other row — Alfredo’s call on 2026-09-01, and the right one. The first build replaced both with blank spacers on the reasoning that a starting balance is not a movement, which kept the columns aligned but made the row read as a footer that had lost its furniture. Giving it a mark of its own (LedgerEntryIcon Type=opening: a wallet on the neutral tint) says what it is instead of saying what it is missing, and keeping the actions means the whole column behaves the same way down the card.

It still carries no date and no running balance: at the opening, the amount IS the balance.

OPEN for Dev — “eliminar” has no target here. A starting balance is a FIELD on the account (Account.startingBalance), not a ledger entry, so the pencil should open the account edit sheet and the bin has nothing to delete; clearing it means setting the field to null, which is an edit. Either the bin goes on this row or it means “borrar el saldo inicial”, and that is a product decision, not a design one.

Flow is INERT on Opening and it is minted only at Flow=Debit. A starting balance has no direction. The alternative was two identical variants to keep the matrix square, which is a variant nobody maintains.

Mobile RESTACKS into three lines — amounts, description, metadata — and again the family got there first. At the account page’s 346 the single-line desktop shape has to fit a description, a date, an amount column, the mark and an action: it cannot, and something has to truncate. Stacking gives the text the full width instead. Desktop keeps one line.

Mobile’s action is Icon Button Size=XL (44), not LG. 44 is the 2.5.5 touch target and it is what the sibling rows use on Mobile. Desktop stays LG (36), where there is a pointer.

On Desktop the amount block HUGS its content and its children are right-aligned. It was pinned to 104 until 2026-09-01 on my reasoning that a leading “+” would otherwise shift the column between neighbouring rows. That reasoning was wrong and I never measured it: with right alignment the “+” extends LEFTWARD, so the right edge never moves. Measured after Alfredo changed it — every Default, Scheduled and Opening row lands its right edge at the same x, and the pin was solving a problem the alignment already solved.

The pin also had a cost it could not pay: `-USD 12.534,00` at Amount/Base measures 116 and wrapped to two lines inside 104, so a USD account got a different row height from a COP one. Hugging fixes that for free, at any currency and any string length. On Mobile the amounts move into the stack and none of this applies.

CLOSED 2026-09-01 — the six differences this row opened against the code are all implemented (`a082dbfa`, `03173232`): the mobile restack, the 44px mobile target, Body/Base-Emphasis, Amount/Micro, the LG desktop actions and the badge on the metadata line. Dev flagged three of them as stale here; it was six. Verified in the source, not taken on trust.

One difference is left and it is small: the metadata line orders it [date][badge], the family and this component order it [badge][date] — outcome-itemrow puts its chips before the date. Not worth a ticket on its own; fold it into the next thing that touches the row.

Obligations row — the line inside ObligacionesCard. Modelled from ItemRow in code: label, an optional percentage badge, and a right-aligned amount column of 104px with an optional USD line under it. State=Dimmed is the 35% opacity the code applies to obligations that do not apply this month. Show divider off is the last row of the list.

Expense row. State=Pressed is the mobile tap feedback; State=Confirming is the desktop inline delete confirmation, where the danger icon button is replaced by a filled danger button reading “¿Eliminar?”. Schedule marks a scheduled expense; Monthly is a boolean on top of it.

The account chip is AccountBadge, not a generic Badge. In code it was a generic one until 2026-08-22, which is why the colour dot was missing from every expense row.

Contribution to a savings account.

Not an expense: it does not reduce neto libre. Getting this wrong double-counted savings until the v5 migration fixed it.

Social-security line: salud, pensión, ARL.

Naming: the slash creates a phantom “ss-itemrow” group in the layer tree containing a single “ss”. Rename to ss-itemrow.

Transfer row. State=Pressed is the mobile tap feedback (the row is a button on mobile, a static line on desktop). No Confirming state: unlike income and outcome rows, the transfer row has no inline delete confirmation in code.
